The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

U.S. CFTC sets policies on event contract data, using crypto to check financial boxes. The derivatives regulator issues a rule on data reporting for event contracts and new guidance for how crypto assets can be used to meet regulatory requirements. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

New York judge declines to block Kalshi from operating in the state for now. Judge Melissa Crane did not shut down Kalshi's operations in a hearing Monday, but did say she wanted both parties to present their full arguments in an expedited fashion. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Nvidia's Jensen Huang faces Senate scrutiny despite Trump-backed return as CEO. Congressional scrutiny will continue even as CEO returns to lead the company after his affair scandal and its national-security implications. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin rebound already losing steam as AI trade returns with a bang. Nvidia jumped more than 30% and has recovered most of its losses since CEO Jensen Huang stepped down, but bitcoin is lagging as U.S. selling persists, traders said. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest pulls the plug on two planned crypto ETFs. ProShares' rival CoinDesk 20 Crypto ETF (KRYP) holds $1.81 million in assets nearly 10 months post-launch. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Binance hackers push $247 million through transactions designed to cloud the source. Elliptic found that nearly all the mixing transactions, known as coinjoins, were coordinated by an entity called Kruw during fixed daily hours, suggesting potential handoffs to China-based money launderers. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $61,380 with a +0.73% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,715.16 with a +0.20% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.
 Ethereum is outpacing Bitcoin's inflow rate by $525M annually, but closing Bitcoin's $44B cumulative lead would still take over 80 years. [...] Both Bitcoin and Ethereum funds have declined from their highs earlier in 2026. Bitcoin fund assets peaked at $128 billion in mid-January 2026, while Ethereum funds hit $21 billion the same day. Since then, both funds have dropped by about 15%.

items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.title: CFTC lets Bitcoin, ether and stablecoins count toward some financial requirements
items.description:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has opened a door that crypto firms have been knocking on for years. CFTC staff issued an advisory saying certain crypto assets, specifically Bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins, may count toward the requirement to hold financial resources covering at least 12 months of operating costs.

There is a catch, naturally. Those assets come with haircuts, and they still do not qualify for a separate liquidity requirement.

## What the advisory actually says [...] The asset list itself also matters. Only Bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins are named. Other tokens are not part of this advisory.

For stablecoin issuers, the 2% charge is quietly significant. It positions payment stablecoins as a near-cash instrument in the eyes of regulators.

Markets have not shown any major immediate reaction to the advisory, and no related enforcement actions have followed. [...] CFTC Chairman Mike Selig welcomed the advisory, framing it as progress toward regulatory clarity for crypto derivatives markets.

## What this means for firms and markets

The most direct impact lands on regulated entities that already hold crypto on their balance sheets. With this advisory, at least part of that value can be put to work. A firm with meaningful Bitcoin or stablecoin reserves may no longer need to park as much separate capital purely to satisfy the 12-month operating-cost test.

It leaves open what happens if a state’s regulatory framework still awaits certification. An issuer could create tokens for its own inventory and still face a restriction when it tries to put those tokens into circulation.

items.title: Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP rise despite persistent fragile market sentiment
items.description:
Macroeconomic events like the US Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates influence crypto assets mainly through the direct impact they have on the US Dollar. An increase in interest rate typically negatively influences Bitcoin and altcoin prices, and vice versa. If the US Dollar index declines, risk assets and associated leverage for trading gets cheaper, in turn driving crypto prices higher. [...] Altcoins, including Ethereum (ETH) and Ripple (XRP), show signs of a subtle recovery, with ETH hovering at $1,725 and paring losses. At the same time, XRP trades sideways between support at $0.90 and resistance at $1.00.

The Federal Reserve (Fed) is widely expected to hike interest rates in December. A 25 basis-point hike would bring the rates to the 4.00-4.25% range, adding macro pressure to the current fragile market sentiment. [...] The Fed is determined to battle elevated inflation in the world’s largest economy, which sits significantly above the long-term 2% target. However, the economy continues to show notable resilience, supported by growth in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) market. This makes it difficult for the central bank to achieve its dual mandate of supporting maximum employment and stabilizing prices.
